question:
If $A=\begin{bmatrix}3&2&1\\ 4&-1&2\\ 7&3&-3\end{bmatrix},$ find $A^{-1}$. Using $A^{-1}$, solve the given system of equations:
$3x+4y+7z=14$
$2x-y+3z=4$
$x+2y-3z=0$
explanation:
**Step 1:** Find the determinant $|A|$ by expanding along Row 1: $|A| = 3(3-6) - 2(-12-14) + 1(12+7) = 3(-3) - 2(-26) + 1(19) = -9 + 52 + 19 = 62$. Since $|A| \neq 0$, $A^{-1}$ exists.

**Step 2:** Find the cofactors of matrix $A$ to construct $\text{adj}(A)$:
$A_{11}=-3, A_{12}=26, A_{13}=19$
$A_{21}=9, A_{22}=-16, A_{23}=5$
$A_{31}=5, A_{32}=-2, A_{33}=-11$
Taking the transpose of the cofactor matrix gives $\text{adj}(A)$:
$\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix}-3&9&5\\26&-16&-2\\19&5&-11\end{bmatrix} \implies A^{-1} = \frac{1}{62}\begin{bmatrix}-3&9&5\\26&-16&-2\\19&5&-11\end{bmatrix}$

**Step 3:** Write the system of linear equations in matrix form as $MX = B$. Notice that the coefficient matrix $M = \begin{bmatrix}3&4&7\\2&-1&3\\1&2&-3\end{bmatrix}$ is the transpose of our matrix $A$ ($M = A^T$). Using the matrix inversion property $(A^T)^{-1} = (A^{-1})^T$, we can isolate $X$:
$X = (A^{-1})^T \cdot B = \frac{1}{62}\begin{bmatrix}-3&26&19\\9&-16&5\\5&-2&-11\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}14\\4\\0\end{bmatrix}$

**Step 4:** Perform the matrix multiplication to calculate the final variables:
$\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{62}\begin{bmatrix}-3(14)+26(4)+0\\9(14)-16(4)+0\\5(14)-2(4)+0\end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{62}\begin{bmatrix}62\\62\\62\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}$. Thus, $x=1, y=1, z=1$.
